thesis: Modern selection is a context-dependent feedback between institutions, reproductive outcomes and transmitted variation.
role: Define fitness, accumulation, trade-offs and valid measurement.

ideas.statement: Reproductive fitness includes descendants surviving and reproducing, not raw child counts.
Cultural transmission can shift quickly while complex genetic traits change more slowly.
A trait has no context-free adaptive value; costs can be linked through pleiotropy or frequency dependence.
Heritability measures variation within an environment and cannot explain national character by itself.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: UK Biobank and Swedish/Norwegian male fertility associations differ.
The hypothetical A/B arithmetic requires perfect transmission and is explicitly unrealistic.
Rice/wheat institutions alter measured psychology rapidly.
Disease variants association lacks robust Mendelian-randomization evidence of disease causing fertility.
Housing and certification can change family timing without genetic intent.
Marriage rules and correlated circumstances change reproductive variance rather than selecting a label in isolation.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Clinical improvement and population robustness are different questions; suffering is not endorsed.
Many popular studies do not establish all steps needed for genetic prediction.
Cross-cultural instruments and ancient evidence cannot provide invented personality scores.

audit.notes: Entire assigned batch read; numbered subchapters covered; no independent citation verification.
